transcript.text: Every so often when I use the hob the electrics in the house go off. Not every time, maybe once a week. It's an induction hob, Hisense I think.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. An intermittent trip is not normal and the hob should not be used again until a qualified appliance/electrical engineer has checked it. The protective device is responding to a possible fault, not simply an overload. With an induction hob, the more likely causes are an insulation/earth-leakage fault in a zone’s coil or power module, its wiring or connection block, or occasionally moisture under the glass after a spill or cleaning. If it only occurs with one zone, that points more towards that zone’s coil/power electronics; if it trips immediately on switching on, the incoming connection or supply side becomes more likely. 1. With the hob isolated at its wall switch or consumer unit, look only for obvious signs around the glass and isolator: recent spills, liquid around the edge of the glass, scorching, or a hot-plastic/burning smell. A spill or cleaning immediately beforehand can support moisture ingress; leave it isolated to dry, but it still needs checking because it has tripped the supply.
2. Note exactly which protective device goes off at the consumer unit and when it happens. Do not keep resetting it to continue cooking. The timing and whether one zone is involved are useful evidence for the engineer. If there is any burning smell, heat damage or scorching, leave it isolated at the hob switch/consumer unit and arrange urgent attention.

candidates: Induction coil, power module or associated wiring developing an earth-leakage fault (high)
Moisture from a spill or cleaning product getting beneath the glass (medium)
Hob supply connection or circuit fault (medium)

reading.symptom: house electrics go off intermittently when using the hob

plan: Safety: a supply trip hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Hisense.
The fault they reported is: "house electrics go off intermittently when using the hob". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
